section.title: Reason for Referral & History of Present Illness

text.paragraph: Reason for Consultation: Mrs. Sophia Rodriguez is a 52-year-old female referred by her primary care physician, Dr. Amanda Clark, MD, for specialist evaluation of recurrent episodic palpitations, sensations of skipped heartbeats, exertional lightheadedness, and a newly detected grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur.

History of Present Illness: The patient reports a 3-month history of awareness of rapid, irregular heartbeats occurring 3 to 4 times per week, typically lasting between 5 to 30 minutes. Symptoms occur both at rest and during mild exertion (e.g., climbing two flights of stairs at work). She denies syncope, chest pressure, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. She notes mild shortness of breath when hurrying up inclines. Has a history of essential hypertension and hyperlipidemia treated with Amlodipine and HCTZ.

list.item: Tobacco Smoking Status: Never smoker (Lifelong non-smoker).
Caffeine Consumption: 2 cups of regular brewed coffee daily (Advised to transition to decaffeinated).
Alcohol Intake: Rare social glass of wine (less than 1 drink per month).
Physical Activity: Moderate aerobic walking 30 minutes 3 days per week.
ECG today confirms normal sinus rhythm with frequent unifocal PVCs without ventricular tachycardia.
Applied 14-day continuous ambulatory ECG Holter patch monitor today to quantify PVC burden and rule out paroxysmal supraventricular arrhythmias.
Initiated low-dose beta-blocker: Metoprolol Tartrate 25 mg PO BID with meals for symptomatic arrhythmia suppression and rate control.
Counseled on reducing dietary caffeine intake and maintaining adequate hydration.

Grade 2/6 crescendo-decrescendo murmur at right upper sternal border. Ordered comprehensive Transthoracic Echocardiogram (TTE) with color Doppler scheduled for 2023-11-16 to evaluate aortic valve morphology, rule out aortic sclerosis/stenosis, and measure left ventricular ejection fraction.

Clinic blood pressure today 134/86 mmHg. Continue current regimen of Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily + Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg PO daily. Metoprolol Tartrate added above will provide additional blood pressure lowering benefit. Continue home BP diary.
Continue Atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily at bedtime. Prior severe myalgias on Simvastatin documented; patient tolerates Atorvastatin without adverse symptoms.

Return to Cardiology Clinic in 4 weeks (2023-12-04 at 10:00 AM) for follow-up consultation with Dr. Vikram Patel to review 14-day continuous Holter monitor telemetry report and Echocardiogram imaging findings.

Instructed on red flag symptoms: Report immediately to Emergency Department or call 911 for prolonged chest pressure, syncope / loss of consciousness, severe sustained tachycardia (> 150 bpm), or severe acute dyspnea.
